picks.title: AI tech detects high-risk coronary inflammation in many asymptomatic patients
picks.excerpt: The first U.S. study of Caristo's FDA-cleared CaRi-Heart AI found about 47% of asymptomatic adults with no detectable coronary plaque had elevated perivascular inflammation on cardiac CT, questioning standard risk assessment tools.
picks.rationale: A clinical finding from an FDA-cleared tool: in its first U.S. study, CaRi-Heart AI showed elevated coronary inflammation in about 47% of asymptomatic adults who had no detectable plaque. That challenges how clinicians stratify cardiac risk. The tagged 10-25 Elucid card was a different company and product (an FFR-CT clearance), not this study. (Swap backfill for the JAMA WISeR letter, whose findings are paywalled.)

picks.title: AI Scribes Improved Note-Taking Time but Not Productivity, Study Finds
picks.excerpt: After clinicians enrolled in the Heidi ambient scribe at Beth Israel Deaconess, median note-active time fell from 21 to 18.6 minutes, but there was no change in same-day or after-hours note closure or clinical productivity (Annals of Internal Medicine).
picks.rationale: A real-world result (Annals of Internal Medicine) that tempers the ambient-scribe hype: notes take less time to write, but notes are not closed sooner and productivity does not change. It speaks directly to health systems deciding on scribe rollouts. This is the single scribe card for the day: the npj adoption cohort and the NEJM AI longitudinal study were set aside.

picks.title: Pennsylvania House passes bill requiring AI disclosure in healthcare
picks.excerpt: If enacted, the legislation would require healthcare facilities, including imaging centers, to disclose their use of AI in clinical decision-making through website postings and written patient notifications.
picks.rationale: A concrete legislative action: a state House vote that would require facilities to tell patients when AI is used in clinical decisions. The 10-15 STAT lobbying card was about lobbying over state rules in general, and the 10-07 Utah card was about sandbox pilots, so this is a distinct event. No other section has claimed it, including politics.

picks.title: Coreline Soft secures FDA clearance for aortic CT software
picks.excerpt: Seoul-based Coreline Soft received FDA 510(k) clearance for Aview Aorta Metrics, AI software that automatically segments the aorta on chest CT, classifies aortic zones and measures each zone's diameter. It is the company's 13th FDA clearance.
picks.rationale: A regulator decision: an FDA 510(k) for automated measurement of aortic diameter by zone on chest CT, from a Korean vendor. The tagged 10-07 AIRS Medical card covered a different company and modality. The 10-10 Coreline card covered a Japanese society certification, not this FDA clearance.

picks.title: AI fails to compensate for night-shift fatigue among residents
picks.excerpt: Radiology residents' chest x-ray accuracy fell significantly after overnight shifts, and AI assistance neither restored pre-shift performance nor meaningfully improved fatigued readers' accuracy, raising patient-safety concerns.
picks.rationale: A patient-safety finding: AI assistance did not restore fatigued residents' chest x-ray accuracy after night shifts, which challenges the idea of AI as a safety net on overnight reads. It differs from the 10-24 meta-analysis of human oversight of erroneous AI and the 10-21 automation-bias card. This is the second AuntMinnie card, which is the outlet cap.
